sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Five players are on DET's latest injury report [ic1]. C Cade Mays (ankle), CB D.J. Reed (hip) and S Kerby Joseph (knee) are Out, while WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) and RB Sione Vaki (ankle) are Questionable. St. Brown takes 30.2% of DET targets [ic8] over 301 team targets [ic9], so if he sits, Jahmyr Gibbs, at 17.6% of targets [ic10], is the likeliest beneficiary. Vaki carries 14.5% of DET rushes [ic11] over 248 team rushes [ic12], so losing him is a small change. TB's latest report lists two players [ic14], with LB Yaya Diaby (knee) Out and WR Emeka Egbuka (foot) Questionable. Egbuka draws 23.4% of TB targets [ic17] over 231 team targets [ic18].

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Motion and play action against TB's pass defense come first. DET uses pre-snap motion on 54.4% of plays [mc1] and play action on 30.3% of dropbacks [mc2], with pass EPA of 0.18 [mc3] against TB's allowed -0.12 [mc4]. TB's secondary has to stay disciplined on motion shifts and play-action fakes. The deep ball is next: DET allows explosives on 9.6% of pass plays [mc5] over 387 plays [mc6], and TB's offense hits them on 5.8% [mc7], so look for the shot off play action that pulls DET's safeties. In the red zone DET allows touchdowns on 67.7% of drives [mc8] over 31 drives [mc9], while TB scores on 50.0% [mc10] over 30 drives [mc11]. Finally, if St. Brown sits, Gibbs and J.Williams each rise to 17.6% [mc13], and Egbuka's 23.4% of TB targets [mc14] gives TB a receiver to attack a secondary already missing Reed and Joseph.
